cuts.cut: B: a run that is over is scanned no more
cuts.why: Measured: median instructions fell 12.8% on sandbox-setup, 9.1% on runner-job and 1.0% on command-check-count, lower in 15, 15 and 14 of 15 rounds, with 46 of 172 starts gone from sandbox-setup's 20 runs. It needs no new mechanism and changes no event. As tried it stops after one empty scan, which has a race: helper scan lists PIDs once and checks each in turn, so a member can fork and exit between the two and leave an empty answer while its child lives; the issue's cut needs two empty scans in a row (one more helper start a run, not measured). As tried it fails one existing test, packages/supervisor/src/supervisor.test.ts 'a cleaned run has no scan of its sandbox still running', in 3 of 3 runs alone (main passes 3 of 3; out/tests.txt): that test needs a timed scan to be running while run.cleaned is recorded (its precondition, 'without one the test shows nothing'), and the cut leaves none to run for a run already drained. The test's guarantee (no scan outlives a cleanup) still holds; its precondition has to be rewritten, which needs an approved proposal, so the cut belongs in an issue of its own and not in a quiet follow-up.
cuts.criterion: A sandboxed run whose first process has exited, and whose sandbox two helper scans in a row found empty (the second begun after the first ended, both begun after that exit), starts no further helper scan, timed or in cleanup: in docs/spikes/2649/measure.mjs starts command-check its cleanup records run.cleaned and process.ended as on main and starts at most 2 helper scans (main: 4), with no timed beat for the run after it; sandbox-setup's median instructions retired over 15 alternated rounds against main (measure.mjs cut) are lower; a run that leaves a forked process behind at its first process's exit is still found, signalled and recorded (tests/acceptance/236's leftover and late-grandchild cases pass unchanged); and supervisor.test.ts's no-scan-after-cleanup case is rewritten, by an approved proposal, to make its timed scan with a run still live, and passes.

cuts.cut: A kept answer for the denial stream's filter, per macOS build
cuts.why: Not tried as a patch. On this Mac (macOS 27.2.1) the subsystem filter never shows the canary, so every supervisor open starts 33 to 36 sandboxed canary probes (about 5.8 G instructions, most of the command check's counted 9.3 G) and a second log stream, and the first sandboxed run waits the warm-up's full 10 s. The first step is finding why the subsystem filter misses here when the Nov 10 audit found it on 27.2. The reports on 27.2.1 carry an empty subsystem (out/hand-e2e.txt, part 3).
cuts.criterion: On a macOS whose sandbox reports don't carry the subsystem com.apple.sandbox.reporting, the second supervisor opened on the same macOS build starts at most 2 canary probes and one log stream before its first sandboxed run, and that run's start call returns (sup.start resolves `started`) within 1 s of being made (docs/spikes/2649/measure.mjs starts command-check, run twice); a refused write in that run is still recorded as sandbox.denied, and supervisor.test.ts's reports-other-subsystem case passes unchanged.

cuts.cut: A: helper scan prints each process's start time, and the beat runs no ps
cuts.why: Measured: no change in instructions retired on the three tasks (median ratios 1.002, 0.999, 1.008), because the counter cannot read ps (setuid root), so what the cut removes was never in the count; on command-check-count it took the median starts of a run from 476 to 340 (the cut removes only ps starts, by construction). Its gain is a start a beat: an idle sandboxed run would start 10 processes a second instead of 20, for as long as it lives; out/ps.json puts a ps -p at 1.85 ms of CPU a start against 1.55 ms for /usr/bin/true, so most of what it saves (about 1.85 ms a beat) is the cost of starting any process. As tried it is macOS only: native/helper-linux.c prints no start, and the patched scanOnce would track nothing on Linux. Worth an issue only with a measure that reads ps, such as the supervisor's CPU time over an idle hour, and with the Linux helper printing the same field.
cuts.criterion: An hour-long idle sandboxed run (docs/spikes/2649/measure.mjs starts idle-hour) starts at most 10.5 processes a second and no /bin/ps after its first process is tracked, on macOS; on Linux, where measure.mjs and the counter don't run, the supervisor starts no ps for a tracked process (a Linux test of its own, which doesn't exist yet); process.tracked carries the same start text as ps -o lstart= under LC_ALL=C for every process of tests/acceptance/236's suites; and the fork-to-process.tracked p95 (measure.mjs latency 200, median of 3 runs) is within 10% of main's read the same way on the same machine at a recorded load.

cuts.cut: Follow a run's forks by kernel event, the marker scan as a slower backstop
cuts.why: Not tried. The helper's watch (kqueue NOTE_FORK and NOTE_EXIT) is built and started for runs with a file limit, but prints only exits: it would have to print each fork it attaches to. Following every sandboxed run with it would see a fork sooner than today's p50 of 113 ms and p95 of 174 ms (read at load 12.8 to 18.8 on 8 cores, above the 50 ms the beat alone explains), and would let the marker scan run far less often than every 100 ms; the scan stays for a process the watch misses (reparented or gone before it was attached), which only it can find. This is the design change the issue's three-way question points to, and the one with the most to gain over hours; it needs its own design pass on the backstop's period and on reading memory_mb.
cuts.criterion: On the same machine and at a recorded load, the fork-to-process.tracked p95 of docs/spikes/2649/measure.mjs latency 200 (median of 3 runs) is at most a quarter of main's read the same way (a target: no watch-based reading exists yet; main read 174 ms on the spike's Mac at load 12.8), an hour-long idle sandboxed run starts at most 1 process a second, and tests/acceptance/236's cases for a grandchild in its own session and group, a process that outlives its parent, and a memory_mb stop pass unchanged.
